h: The Mind Game Behind a Fast Lap
p: Here's the thing nobody tells you about karting: half of it happens in your head. The drivers who post the quickest times aren't always the bravest. They're the calmest. They look ahead, pick a line and stick to it, and they don't panic when someone's breathing down their neck.

A good way to get there is to break the lap into chunks. Work out the two or three corners where you're losing the most time and focus on those. Small improvements in the trickiest bends add up quickly, and you'll see the difference on the timing screen.
Most of all, relax. Tense arms make for twitchy steering, and twitchy steering is slow. Take a breath on the straights.

A final tip: don't overthink it on your very first session. Learn the layout, enjoy the speed and save the serious lap-hunting for your second race. Most people find their times tumble once the track feels familiar and the nerves have settled down.

East London gives you plenty to do once the race is over. Hop on a Thames Clipper from Canary Wharf for a river trip, or head across to Greenwich, where the Cutty Sark, the Royal Observatory and Greenwich Park are all within easy walking distance of each other.
